news.summary: England's pacers cleaned up Pakistan in 34 overs after the visitors' top five batters failed to score double figures.

news.title: Fachin cancela sessão no STF após Dino reintegrar Andrei
news.summary: Retorno do diretor-geral da corporação ao cargo contraria decisão de André Mendonça de 3ª feira (8.set) que determinou o afastamento

news.title: Pope merchandise flies off shelves as France gears up for pontiff's visit
news.summary: Tshirts, mugs and rosaries... These are just a few of the items available in the range of merchandise hitting souvenir shops ahead of Pope Leo XIV’s much anticipated visit to the northeastern French city of Metz on 28th September. The items have proved hugely popular, with some flying off the shelves quicker than shopkeepers can stock them.

news.title: Modern warfare: Ukraine racing to develop new interceptor drones
news.summary: In recent weeks, Russia has been deploying jet-powered Shahed-type drones against Ukraine, presenting a new challenge for Ukrainian air defences. Kyiv is now working to develop interceptor drones capable of matching their speed and bringing them down. FRANCE 24’s Gulliver Cragg is in Kielce, Poland, at one of Europe’s largest arms fairs. He is joined by Roman Hapachylo, CEO of DoD Solution, one of the companies developing these technologies.

news.title: 12 countries including France, UK and Canada to sanction Israeli settlements
news.summary: Twelve countries including Britain, Canada and France announced Tuesday they would sanction trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, after increasing attacks by settlers against Palestinians in the occupied territory. Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, and Sweden also plan to issue restrictions on trade with the settlements, the nations' foreign ministers said in a joint statement. The action follows weeks of increasing attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the illegally occupied territory that has drawn widespread condemnation from the international community.

news.title: Governo marca leilão do aeroporto de Brasília para 17 de dezembro
news.summary: Concessionária que vencer disputa terá de assumir outros 10 terminais regionais

news.title: Dino diz que decisão de Mendonça sobre Andrei beneficia investigados
news.summary: Na decisão, o ministro afastou a hipótese de atribuir intenção deliberada ao colega de STF ou a qualquer outro agente público

news.title: Greetings from Paris, where the 2024 Olympics balloon rises again
news.summary: The floating Olympic cauldron, held aloft by a giant glowing balloon, is still making regular appearances two years after the 2024 Paris Games, showing up all summer long in the nighttime Paris sky.

news.title: Putin and Trump discuss Ukraine in 'extremely frank' call
news.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and US counterpart Donald Trump on Tuesday discussed the Ukraine conflict in an "extremely frank" and constructive hour-long phone call, the Kremlin said. It came after US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visited Moscow and Kyiv over the weekend in an attempt to kickstart long-stalled US efforts to end the fighting. Washington has been pushing for fresh face-to-face talks between Moscow and Kyiv.

news.title: 'We need to put the tech bros back in their box,' says Baroness Beeban Kidron
news.summary: In this edition, one of the world’s leading campaigners against the increasing influence of Big Tech describes it as “generational injustice against children”. Baroness Beeban Kidron abandoned her thirty-year career as a world-renowned filmmaker, to challenge Big Tech, though she says it’s not necessarily the technology that is at fault, but the way we use it. In conversation with FRANCE 24’s Stuart Norval, she talks about her book “Users – How big tech took control and How to Fight back”.

news.title: Suspected migrant smugglers go on trial in Paris over mass drowning in Channel
news.summary: Fourteen people went on trial in France on Tuesday over the death of at least 31 people in the Channel in 2021, the deadliest accident involving asylum seekers trying to reach the English coast. The trial carries particular significance because of the high death toll and the sheer number of civil parties involved, 114 in all, including victims' families. Some of them travelled from Erbil in Iraq's Kurdistan region to testify.

news.title: Syria arms depot explosion kills at least 14
news.summary: The explosion struck near the Syrian city of Sarmada in Idlib province in the northwest. The Defense Ministry said the weapons and remnants from the war were being stored temporarily at the site before being relocated.

news.title: French Riviera heist: Renoir paintings stolen from French museum
news.summary: Police were on Tuesday hunting for two thieves who escaped with two Renoir paintings from a museum in southern France, after abandoning two others in its garden as they fled, a mayor said. The heist is the latest in a string of such robberies in France including the daylight theft last year of crown jewellery valued at around $100 million from the Louvre in Paris.

news.title: France’s record heatwave pushes champagne alcohol levels to historic high
news.summary: France’s record-breaking summer heat has forced champagne producers to contend with unusually high sugar levels in grapes, forcing authorities to allow alcohol content of up to 15 percent in the region’s sparkling wine for the first time. Champagne is usually capped at 13 percent.

news.title: Dortmund’s Karetsas hospitalised after collapsing in Champions League match
news.summary: Greek teenage star Konstantinos Karetsas faced 'circulatory problems' and was stretchered off during the match against Villarreal.

news.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, September 9: British papers are reacting to the sanctions imposed on Israel. Next: Israeli papers discuss Haaretz's October 7 revelatory investigation. Also: CDs are back! Finally, South Park renames itself to South America to mock Trump.

news.title: Nigeria, Boko Haram reportedly reach secret three-month ceasefire
news.summary: The reported truce follows the release of 360 villagers abducted during a Boko Haram attack in northeastern Nigeria.

news.title: Rungis market chief on supply chains and feeding the world
news.summary: In today’s edition, FRANCE 24’s Delano D'Souza speaks with the man at the heart of France's food supply chain. Stéphane Layani is the head of the Rungis wholesale food market – the largest of its kind in Europe – and chairman of the World Union of Wholesale Markets. Earlier this year Layani came out with a book titled Le Monde a faim, or "The World is Hungry" in English. In his interview, he gives his perspective on how France's food system will transform in the coming years.

news.title: Cambodia's floating schools hit by rising fuel costs
news.summary: The Iran war has sent fuel prices higher in Cambodia, squeezing families who rely on fishing and boats for their livelihoods. For children living on Tonle Sap, rising fuel costs pose yet another barrier to education.
